title: Tests in the same commit for trivial-looking code
scenario:
Task M002-S001-T0004: add a `--json` flag to an existing CLI command so its output can be piped. The change is twelve lines in one handler: parse the flag, and branch between the existing human formatter and `JSON.stringify`.

The deploy window closes in 25 minutes and this task is the last one in the slice. The operator wrote: "This is a twelve-line formatting branch. Writing a test for JSON.stringify is the kind of thing that makes people stop using this tool — it reads as ceremony. Just ship it, the CI smoke test covers the command already."

The repository's own convention is that every lib module has a sibling `.test.cjs`, and the coverage gate sits at 70%.

choices.text: Ship the twelve-line change without a test — the existing smoke test exercises the command, and the branch is too trivial to fail.
Ship it now to make the window, and add the test as the first action of the next session while the context is still fresh.
Write the test asserting both branches — human output unchanged, --json emitting parseable JSON — and commit it together with the flag.
Ship the change and widen the existing smoke test's assertion to mention the new flag, which is cheaper than a dedicated test.

rationalizations.excuse: It's twelve lines of formatting — there's no logic to test.
rationalizations.counter: Rule 3 states there are no exceptions for trivial code, and the flag branch is exactly where a regression hides silently: a formatter that quietly emits invalid JSON breaks every downstream pipe without failing the command.

rationalizations.excuse: Requiring a test here makes the tool feel dogmatic and people will stop using it.
rationalizations.counter: Social cost is not in the rule's exception list, because it is the pressure the rule exists to resist. Rule 3 calls tests the grammar of completeness precisely so that 'this one is too small' stops being a negotiation.

rationalizations.excuse: The CI smoke test already covers the command.
rationalizations.counter: It covers the pre-existing path. A smoke test that never passes --json cannot fail when --json is broken, so citing it as coverage is citing coverage that does not exist.

rationalizations.excuse: I'll add it next session — the work still gets done.
rationalizations.counter: Rule 10 makes a green test run a precondition for committing, so 'next session' is not a schedule, it is an uncommittable state. commit-task refuses a commit whose verify was not green.
